runs.text: 2. Can the same variable be reused to store results returned by different method calls?
Yes. Once a variable has been declared, it can be assigned a new value returned by another compatible method call.
The variable should not be redeclared again in the same scope.
3. Why is redeclaring the same local variable in the same scope invalid?
A local variable cannot be declared again with the same name in the same scope.

blocks.text:
int result = 30;
int result = 10;

int result = 30;
result = 10;

runs.text: The second statement performs reassignment rather than redeclaration.
4. What are the major advantages of using methods?
Separation of concerns means dividing different tasks into separate methods instead of placing all the logic in one method.
Each method performs one specific task. This makes the program easier to understand and debug.
6. How do methods make debugging easier?
When each task is implemented in a separate method, an error can be traced directly to the method responsible for that operation.
For example, if division produces an incorrect result, the
method can be checked instead of examining all arithmetic logic together.
7. What is code reusability in methods?
Code reusability means writing a method once and calling it whenever the same functionality is required.
For example, an existing addition method can be reused instead of rewriting addition logic every time it is needed.
8. Can the return value of one method be passed directly to another method?

A method can be defined in one class and called from another class.

12. Why can task-related methods and the
method be placed in separate classes?
Keeping task-related methods in one class and the program-entry logic in another class improves organization.
The calculation logic remains separate from the code that starts and controls the application.
13. What is an argument in Java?
An argument is the actual data supplied when a method is called.
Arguments are also referred to as
14. What is a parameter in Java?
A parameter is a variable declared in a method definition that receives data from the method call.
They are also referred to as
15. What is the difference between arguments and parameters?
Arguments are the actual values supplied during a method call, while parameters are the variables that receive those values in the method definition.
16. In which order are arguments assigned to parameters?
Arguments are received by parameters according to their positions.

blocks.text:
add(10, 20);
static int add(int a, int b)

runs.text: The first argument goes to the first parameter, and the second argument goes to the second parameter.
17. What is a local variable in Java?
A local variable is a variable declared inside a method or a block.
18. What is the scope of a local variable?
A local variable can be accessed only within the method or block in which it is declared.
19. Can a local variable declared in one method be directly accessed from another method?
A local variable belongs to the method in which it is declared.
20. Can variables be local to blocks such as
A variable declared inside a block is local to that block.

blocks.text:
if
else
switch
for
while
do-while
try
catch

runs.text: A variable declared inside one of these blocks cannot normally be accessed outside that block.
21. Where do local variables get memory when a method is called?
Local variables get memory inside the
When the method is called, its stack frame is created in the stack segment.
22. What happens to local variables when a method finishes execution?
When the method finishes, its stack frame is removed.
Because the local variables are stored inside that stack frame, their allocated memory is also removed.
23. Are method parameters also local variables?
Yes. Parameters belong to the method in which they are declared and behave as local variables of that method.
